case: A seat proposes P-1 (the laptop's clock kept UTC), a proposition under test; question 1's answer assumes it only conditionally; the operator admits it as a given; question 2's answer then assumes it outright.
design: docs/adr/0011 'Premises': a premise is a P-n on the question chain with its words verbatim, where they stand, its authority, scope, revision and class; only the operator's are givens (the goal's front matter, the register's premise add, the console); a given is not proved again and is never an open part.

docs/adr/0011 'Premises': an agent's premise_propose is a proposition under test until the operator admits it (premise admit P-n --as given|supplied_assertion); until then an answer assumes it only conditionally ("assuming P-n"), and the admission changes its class, not its revision.

docs/adr/0011 'Premises': an answer cites premises [{id, rev, stance: assumed | supported | contradicted | unresolved, refs?}], present-only in the ledger's hashed core; an answer that cites none reads as before.
docs/adr/0013 'The end of a run, under every stop policy': done finishes a run when every question has a disposition under the bar; a warning never holds.
